337.h: The University of Ilorin (UNILORIN) is a federal public research university, established by decree of the Federal Military Government in August 1975. It began as a university college affiliated to the University of Ibadan. Its first principal, the historian T. N. Tamuno, left within months to become vice-chancellor of Ibadan, and Professor O. O. Akinkugbe, a former dean of medicine at Ibadan, took over. With support from successive military governors of Kwara State, who gave the college part of the Kwara State College of Technology's land, the first 200 students were admitted after an entrance examination on 23 October 1976, and lectures began two days later. The college became a fully autonomous university in October 1977, with Akinkugbe as its first vice-chancellor.
337.a: UNILORIN started with three faculties, Arts, Science and Education, on a temporary 'mini-campus' borrowed from Kwara State Polytechnic. It now has 16 faculties and more than 100 academic departments offering 103 programmes, and it enrols more international students than any other Nigerian university.
337.c: The main campus in Ilorin, Kwara State, covers about 5,000 hectares, making it the largest university campus in Nigeria by land area and one of the largest in Africa.

256.h: The Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB) was established on 1 January 1988, when the Federal Government separated four universities of technology it had merged into older universities in 1984. The demerger created Nigeria's first two universities of agriculture, at Abeokuta and Makurdi. The Abeokuta institution had begun in 1983 as the Federal University of Technology, Abeokuta, and between 1984 and 1988 it was the College of Science and Technology, Abeokuta, under the University of Lagos.
256.a: FUNAAB is organised into colleges rather than faculties. It started with five, covering agricultural management and rural development, animal science and livestock production, environmental resources management, and the natural sciences. The natural sciences college was later split into physical sciences, biological sciences, and plant science and crop production, and colleges of engineering and veterinary medicine were added in March 2002. A college of food science followed in the 2008/2009 session.
256.c: The university started on the old campus of Abeokuta Grammar School at Isale-Igbein, near the city centre, and completed its move to its permanent site on Alabata Road, Abeokuta, in 1997.

282.h: Kaduna State University (KASU) is a public university created under a Kaduna State law of May 2004, to expand higher education in both the north and south of the state. Governor Ahmed Mohammed Makarfi appointed Professor Idris Abdulkadir as its first pro-chancellor and Professor Abubakar Sani Sambo, later head of the Energy Commission of Nigeria, as its first vice-chancellor. The emir and former central bank governor Sanusi Lamido Sanusi has served as its pro-chancellor.
282.a: KASU has sixteen faculties and more than 50 departments. The Kaduna campus opened first with basic degree programmes.
282.c: From the start, the university was given two campuses, one in Kaduna city and one in Kafanchan in southern Kaduna State, so that students in both halves of the state are within reach of a university.

305.h: Nile University of Nigeria (NUN) is a private university founded in 2009 in Abuja. It opened with three faculties, Arts and Social Sciences, Engineering, and Natural and Applied Sciences, and 93 students. In July 2020 it was acquired by Honoris United Universities, a pan-African education group backed by the investment firm Actis, making it the group's first institution in West Africa alongside members in Tunisia, Morocco, Mauritius, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia. It has since grown to more than 13,000 students.
305.a: The university has eight faculties and a School of Postgraduate Studies, offering 34 undergraduate and 47 postgraduate programmes. Its engineering faculty covers computer, electrical and electronics, civil, petroleum and gas, chemical, mechanical, mechatronics and information and communication engineering, several of them up to doctoral level. The sciences include biology, biotechnology, biochemistry and microbiology. A Centre for Lifelong Learning runs short professional courses. It is accredited by the National Universities Commission.
305.c: The university occupies a 113-hectare campus in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory.

280.h: Ignatius Ajuru University of Education (IAUE) is a public university owned by the Rivers State Government and devoted to the training of teachers. It began in June 1971 as Rivers State College of Education and kept that name until October 2009. The college became an autonomous body with its own governing council in the 1970s, with Mr E. Aguma as its first provost in 1975. Its official opening and first graduation ceremony, for 462 students, took place on 11 March 1978. The National Universities Commission records its establishment as a university in 2010.
280.a: IAUE awards degrees in education across arts, sciences, social sciences and vocational subjects, preparing graduates to teach in Nigerian schools.
280.c: The institution moved to its permanent site at Rumuolumeni, Port Harcourt, in January 1977.

230.h: Bells University of Technology, also called Bellstech, was Nigeria's first private university of technology. It was founded by the Bells Educational Foundation, which already ran nursery, primary and secondary schools and is owned by former President Olusegun Obasanjo. The foundation received its licence from the National Universities Commission on 9 June 2005, and teaching began on 1 July 2005. The university was set up to link theoretical education with practical technology, and to produce graduates with technical and entrepreneurial skills.
230.a: As a university of technology, Bells concentrates on engineering, the sciences, technology and related management programmes.
230.c: The university is located in Ota, Ogun State, close to the Lagos border.

288.h: Kwara State University (KWASU) is a public research university owned by the Kwara State Government. Planning began on 11 July 2007, when Governor Bukola Saraki inaugurated a committee led by former governor Mohammed Shaaba Lafiagi. The university's law was signed on 24 December 2008, and the National Universities Commission issued its licence on 9 February 2009. Its pioneer vice-chancellor, Professor Abdul Rasheed Na'Allah, had chaired African American Studies at Western Illinois University in the United States, and the diplomat Ibrahim Gambari was its first chancellor. From the start it was designed to emphasise community service and entrepreneurship as well as teaching and research.
288.a: KWASU has about 60 academic departments in 11 faculties. In July 2019 it opened the Muhammadu Buhari Library, described at the time as one of the best university libraries in West Africa.
288.c: The main campus is at Malete, near Ilorin. When fully developed the university is planned to operate from three campuses, at Malete, Ilesha-Baruba and Osi-Opin.
